judgements.justification: One of B's Reviewer_c6Mx's criticisms behind its 4 was wrong: the weakly convex n^{-1/4} rate matches the best non-private rate, so its gap to the smooth case shows nothing; no A criticism rested on such an error.
A's chair gave a spotlight over 7, 6, 7 at confidence 2 to 4 with no reviewer above 7 or arguing for a higher tier, on the chair's own reading.
A's Reviewer_Dzyq gave a 7 with three generic paragraphs and no specific point, and it counted toward A's no-detractor 6.67 mean.
The authors revealed no flaw on one forum only; the Theorem 10 error was found by A's reviewer, and the weaker rate against [ZCH+20] is stated in the paper.
The one flaw found, the d-decreasing Theorem 10 term, was fixed with a refined bound that Reviewer_vTqw accepted after checking, not on trust.
In A, Reviewer_vTqw raised its score to 7 after the rebuttal; in B no reviewer replied and c6Mx's 4 stood.
Only B raised the incrementality of the GLL result, the novelty of the private Frank-Wolfe, the missing lower bounds and the implicit projection oracle; no A reviewer questioned novelty.
Both committees flagged the fragmented, loosely connected results; A's chair ignored it and gave a spotlight, while B's chair made it the only stated concern and stopped at poster.
B's chair followed the split panel's scores and a concern several reviewers shared, not one reviewer's position.
No reviewer cited other reviews as the reason for a score change.
The authors answered every reviewer's point in both committees; no misreading or missed follow-up held a score down.
A's Reviewer_KmGd (2 h, confidence 2, three lines) and Reviewer_Dzyq (no specific point) never replied to the rebuttal, and their 6 and 7 counted unchallenged in A's spotlight.
B accepted as a poster in line with its split ratings; no chair went below its majority.
Neither chair stated a positive view and then decided by a score threshold.
c6Mx's 4 rests on incrementality of the core GLL result, which is central, not peripheral.
Both committees read the paper as a theory paper on private optimisation rates.
A's only reviewer who moved, vTqw, had confidence 4 and checked the bound; the low-confidence reviewers did not move.
B's extra demands (lower bounds, experiments, novelty of technique) are issues A never raised, covered by R07, not a different bar for the same paper type.
No reviewer's praise rested on a wrong factual claim.
c6Mx did not reply to the rebuttal, so no reviewer acknowledged an answered concern and kept the score.
B accepted without refusing to credit promised revisions; neither committee made promises the deciding issue.
No reviewer stated a changed stance without editing the score.
B's chair mentions unrecorded discussion but no additional reviewer.
Clarity complaints came from both committees and were not tied to distance from the field.
TpjV's edit does not expose the earlier rating, and no raised score contradicts its own text.
B counted its detractor c6Mx's 4; A had no detractor to set aside.
The only rating above 7 was B's Reviewer_MuL7's 8, in the lower-tier committee, so a champion did not lift the higher tier.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading.
No reviewer contested the paper's premise from another theoretical tradition.
A's meta-review says the paper 'pushes forward the research' and recommends it 'be accepted', giving no reason for a spotlight.

B's c6Mx and TpjV tied the results to [FKT20], [ZCH+20] and variance-reduced Frank-Wolfe and judged novelty against them, while A's reviewers asked clarifications and heard the [ZCH+20] comparison only from the authors.
No meta-review contradicts the forum record about reviewers' final positions.
Brcd's remark on venue fit came with a 7 and did not cap B's tier; no one argued narrow audience.
B's detractor c6Mx was mostly correct, and B's chair followed the scores rather than arguing against a misreading.

reasoning: A's spotlight rests on three accept-side ratings with two thin reviews and a chair who gave no case for the tier (R02, R03, R12, R30), while B drew confident reviewers who knew the prior work and raised incrementality issues A never saw (R07, R31). Both committees saw the fragmented presentation but weighed it differently (R08), and only A's scores moved after the rebuttal (R06). One of c6Mx's criticisms was factually wrong (R01). The stage 1 candidates (AC tier above scores, novelty detractor only in B, simple technique as advance or corollary, fragmentation penalised by B's AC, thin reviews in A) all map to existing reasons, so no reason is added.
